transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Well, I came in today because... I just can't stop seeing this sagging, uneven spot right around my jaw and my neck. It's just really bothering me. Even when folks tell me it looks normal, I just can't see it that way. I feel like it’s the very first thing the families I work for, the nurses, or the people at my church notice when they look at me.
How much time would you say you spend each day thinking about or checking this spot on your jaw and neck?

It takes up a good amount of time, honestly. Um, especially in the mornings. Right before I leave for work or go to a meeting, I just keep going back to the bathroom mirror. I'll stand there fixing my collar and adjusting my hair around my neck, trying to see how it looks. Then I'll pull out my phone and take another look in the camera. I even end up asking my daughter if it looks strange to her. It's... well, it's actually made me late more than once because I just keep checking and fixing it.

Besides being late to work or meetings because of the checking, has this concern about your jaw and neck affected other areas of your life—like your relationships, your job performance, or your ability to enjoy things you normally would?

Well, yes, it has. At work, I've actually passed up a few chances to help lead meetings or take on some supervisory duties. I just... I worry that if I'm up there, everyone will just be staring at my face and neck. And honestly, I've even fallen behind on my paperwork a few times because I get stuck in the bathroom trying to make myself look presentable before I can focus. 

Outside of work, it's affected me too. I used to go to a book club and a walking club, but lately, I've just stopped going to some of those activities. The whole process of getting ready and trying to hide my neck... it just feels like too much effort, so I just stay home instead.

When you're checking the mirror or adjusting your neck and hair, do you feel like you *have* to do it—like you can't resist the urge—even though you might want to stop? Or is it more that you genuinely believe you need to check because you're worried about how it looks?

I think it's more that I genuinely believe I need to check it. I mean, I'm worried about how it looks, so I feel like I have to make sure it's covered up or looking okay before I can go anywhere. It's not like a... like a physical urge I can't control, it's just that if I don't check it, I'll be anxious the whole time thinking everyone is staring at it. So I just have to look.
Do you think your worry about how your jaw and neck look might be more intense or out of proportion compared to what other people seem to notice or be concerned about?

Well, I suppose it might be. I mean, that's why I came in, really. I just can't stop seeing this sagging, uneven spot around my jaw and neck. My family and the people I work with tell me it looks normal, but... I just don't see what they see. To me, it feels like it's the very first thing families, the nurses at work, or even people at church notice when they look at me. So, yes, maybe my worry is bigger than what they actually see, but it feels very real to me.

If I told you that several doctors examined your jaw and neck and found nothing abnormal or wrong with it, would you be able to believe them, or would you still be convinced that there's something wrong with how it looks?

I don't know. I mean, I hear what you're saying, but... I think I'd still have a hard time believing it. If a bunch of doctors told me it was fine, I might try to tell myself they're right, but... when I look in the mirror, I still see it. I still see the sagging. So, even if they said nothing was wrong, I think I'd still feel like it looks awful. It's just hard to ignore what I see with my own eyes, you know?

When you're not actively looking in the mirror or thinking about your appearance, do intrusive thoughts about your jaw and neck pop into your head unbidden—like unwanted thoughts you're trying to push away? Or is it more that you're mainly worried about how others perceive you based on your appearance?

I don't think they really pop in out of nowhere. It's not like a thought I'm trying to fight off or push away. It's definitely more the second thing you said—I'm just worried about how other people are seeing me. 

If I'm at work, I just... I know it's there, and I'm worrying if the people I'm helping are staring at my jaw and my neck. So it's not really random thoughts forcing their way in. It's mostly just that constant worry about how I look to everyone else.
